JUDGMENT
The Police Inspector-03 Sri. K. S. Muniyappa from the Karnataka Lokayukta, Bengaluru Urban
Division has charge-sheeted the accused for offences punishable under Section 13(1)(e) r/w 13(2) of
The Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (for short, the P.C Act) and Sections 465 and 471 of IPC in
Crime No.31/2014.
2. Allegations in brief are that, the accused was a public servant and working as the Assistant
Executive Engineer, KSRTC Head Office at Shanthi Nagara, Bengaluru City. The check period
applicable to him is 25.08.1989 to 29.03.2014. During the said period, the accused had accumulated
the total assets worth Rs.61,45,944/- (29.84%) disproportionate to his known sources of an income
worth Rs.2,05,90,607.00. The accused has created and forged the documents with an intention to

cheat. Having failed to give the satisfactory accounts therefor, the accused has committed the afore-
referred offences.
3. After taking cognizance of the offence, the case was got registered by this Court. The presence of
the accused was secured. He was represented by a counsel and got enlarged on the bail. After the
complying the requirement under Section 207 of Cr.P.C., this court has framed the charge against
the accused for offences 4 Spl. C.C.456/2017 punishable under Section 13(1)(e) read with Section
13(2) of the PC Act and Sections 465 & 471 of IPC, read over and explained the same in the language
known to him. He pleaded not guilty, but claims to be tried. Hence, the trial of the case was fixed.
4. To prove its allegations, the prosecution has examined 17 witnesses as PW1 to 17 and got marked
documents as per Ex.P1 to P130. After closure of the prosecution evidence, and getting compliance
of Section 437(A), the accused has been examined under Section 313 of the Code of Criminal
Procedure. Having denied the incriminating circumstances appearing against him in the evidence of
the prosecution witnesses to be false, the accused has adduced the evidence as DW1 apart examining
his 4 witnesses as Dw.2 to 5. He has got marked documents as per Ex.D1 to 20 in support of his
defence that, he is an innocent.
5. Heard arguments from the learned Public Prosecutor and the defence arguments with reference
to the written arguments from the learned counsel for the accused. After going through the record,
the following points would arise for the consideration.
1. Does the prosecution prove beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused was a public 5 Spl.
C.C.456/2017 servant?
2. Does the prosecution prove beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused had accumulated the
assets worth Rs.61,45,944/- (29.84%) disproportionate to his known sources of an income during
his check period and thereby committed an offence punishable under Section 13(1)(e) r/w Section
13(2) of the PC Act, 1988?
3 Does the prosecution prove beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused had dishonestly and
fraudulently prepared and submitted the bills worth Rs.62,28,480/- and Rs.25,95,000/-
respectively by using them to be genuine bills and thereby committed offences punishable under
Sections 465 and 471 of IPC?
6. Point No.1 and 2 are answered in the affirmative and 3 in the negative for the following :
REASONS
7. Point No.1 : It is not in dispute that, the accused was working as the Assistant Executive Engineer
in the head office of KSRTC at Shanthi Nagara, Bengaluru as on the date of the raid. He was a public
servant as defined 6 Spl. C.C.456/2017 under Section 2(c) of the PC Act. The Lokayukta Police have
conducted the raid upon the house and other places of the accused on 29.03.2014. In view of these
admitted facts, the status of the accused as a public servant does not warrant the further discussion.

8. PW1 - Sri. V. P. M. Swamy, the Dy.S.P from the Karnataka Lokayukta of Bengaluru Urban
Division deposed to have conducted the preliminary enquiry on the assets of the accused and
submitted the source report vide Ex.P1 dated 21.03.2014. PW7 Sri. C. W. Poovaiah, the then Dy.S.P
states to have got registered the FIR as per Ex.P70 dated 28.03.2014 against the accused under the
order of the Superintendent of the Police concerned. His evidence reveals that, the search was
conducted upon the house of the accused as per the mahazar at Ex.P3 under the warrant of this
Court. PW8 Dr. Anil Kumar P. G., the Police Inspector states that, he has conducted the search in
the office of the accused as per Ex.P5 under the warrant of this Court. PW3 Sri. M. Suresh and PW5
Smt. L. Kavya - the official pancha witnesses admits their presence at the places of search and
identifies their signatures in the mahazars at Ex.P3 and 5 respectively.
9. The Police Inspector PW10 Sri. K. S. Muniyappa (for short, the IO) deposes that, he has
undertaken and completed the investigation. Himself has laid the charge-

public servant had acquired the assets disproportionate to his known sources of an income during
the check period from 25.08.1989 to 29.03.2014 as hereunder. That apart, the accused forged
certain documents with an intention to cheat the Government.

10. Whereas, the accused denies the said allegations as baseless. He asserts that, he is an innocent
and has not committed any offence as alleged. His counsel has advanced the oral arguments with
reference to his written arguments. According to him, the accused is an innocent and the Police have
falsely registered the present case based on an inflated the assets rather than, filing the 'B' report for
want of evidence to constitute the ingredients of alleged offences.
11. Generally, and even as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Krishna Reddy Vs. State by
the Dy.S.P., Hyderbad reported as (1992) 4 SCC 45 and Vasanth Rao Huge Vs. State of M. P
reported as (2017) 14 8 Spl. C.C.456/2017 SCC 442, the burden is on the prosecution to prove the
offence of criminal misconduct, rather than expecting the accused to prove his defence. However, in
the case of Subhas Kharate Vs. State of M. P reported as 2000 KLJ 1178 and AIR 1973 SC 2773 in the
case of Kali Ram Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh, it was held that, once the prosecution discharges its
burden, giving scope to raise the statutory presumption, the onus shifts upon the accused to rebut
such presumption based on the preponderance of probabilities. Also referred AIR 1979 SC 1455 in
the case of Mansingh Vs. Delhi Administration. With this background, the offence in question
against the accused needs to decide with reference to the material evidence on his assets,
expenditure and the income.

13. That, the value of the above assets under 57 heads would be Rs.1,82,06,338/-, but not
Rs.1,83,60,409/- as calculated by the IO. The accused in his written arguments dated 24.01.2025
admits the value of assets at Sl. No.4, 6, 13 Spl. C.C.456/2017 7, 9, 10, 12 to 42, 44 to 57 worth
Rs.46,82,895/-. Thus, the worth of assets at Sl. No.1 to 3, 5, 8, 11 and 43 are in serious dispute.
Hence, the appreciation of evidence on each asset is as hereunder :
14. Asset No.1 : is a site bearing No.27 with the dimension of 15 x 40 feet. The allegation that, it was
purchased by the accused for Rs.66,000/- in the name of his wife - Smt. Y. Rathnamma under the
sale deed dtd: 09.01.2004 as per the sale deed at Ex.P78. But, in his 13(A) schedule statement, the
accused states that, his wife has purchased the site out of her savings from the tailoring business and
the rent from the house in site No.6. Admittedly, she was a house wife and has not been examined in
this case to prove her source of income. It is not in dispute that, a sewing machine was found in the
house of the accused at the time of search by the Police. The accused has not placed any material to
prove the independent source for his wife to save prior to 2004. If really, she was earning from the
tailoring to the extent of purchasing the property, she should have certainly maintained the account
to that extent as rightly argued by the learned Public Prosecutor. Thus, in the absence of such
evidence, mere possessing the sewing machine in the house for the personal purpose would not be a
ground to presume the income.
14 Spl. C.C.456/2017
i) As per the sale deed at Ex.P80 dtd 09.01.2004, the accused was the owner of site No.6 (House
No.205). He asserts as if DW3 Sri. Chinnappa Reddy being the adopted father of his wife has
purchased the site in her name. But, there is no even an iota of document or supporting
circumstance to prove it. That apart, his wife was not the owner of site No.6 as on 09.01.2004 prior
to its sale to the accused. Rather, she sold this site to the accused as a GPA holder of one G. Laxman.
Interestingly, neither the contents of so called GPA nor the contents of the sale deed at Ex.P80 dtd
09.01.2004 discloses the existence of building or structure of any kind in the site as on its sale.
Therefore, the contention of the accused that, his wife was having rental income from the house in
site No.6 to purchase asset No.1 on 09.01.2004 itself is unacceptable.
ii) It is not in dispute that, a building with the ground + three floors was constructed at site No.27 in
the year 2004 itself. PW6 Sri. M. C. Boregowda was the Assistant Executive Engineer from the
PWD. He states to have assessed the cost of its construction at Rs.10,03,772/- and issued the report
vide Ex.P6. On the other hand, the accused in his 13(A) schedule states to have spent Rs.5,92,000/-
only towards the construction. Having contradicted the same, the accused in his evidence at para 6
claims that, he spent Rs.6,44,000/- only. He finds fault with the report of PW6 on the basis of his
cross-

iii) However, in his written arguments, the accused admits the cost of construction at
Rs.10,03,772/-. But, his grievance is that, he was a qualified civil engineer. The whole construction
of the building was taken place under his self supervision. Therefore, according to him, PW6 should
have deducted the construction cost at 10% towards the self supervision and another 10% towards
the overhead charges, in all 20% at Rs.2,00,754/-. With this, his contention is that, the IO should
have considered the total construction cost of this building at Rs.8,03,018/- rather than
Rs.10,03,772/-.
iv) Thus, the difference amount of Rs.2,00,754/- is in dispute. As per the service record of the
accused, basically he is an electrical diploma holder and working as the Electrical Engineer even as
on the date of raid. No supporting evidence is on record to prove his service on the construction side
during the check period. The fact is that, as a public servant, he was to ensure his presence in the 16
Spl. C.C.456/2017 office from morning till evening on all working days. Therefore, the question that
arise is, as to how can he invest his official time and supervise the construction of his own
buildings?. In fact, the person who undertook the work of construction is competent to speak as to,
who has supervised it. But, not examined the said person by the accused. Therefore, I am to discard
the defence contention to that extent. The construction of ground + three floors in the area of 15 x
40 sq. ft in the year 2004 at the cost of less than the amount considered by the IO cannot be
expected. With these observations, I am to hold that, the cost of construction at Rs.10,03,772/-
stands proved. Thus, if the admitted purchase value of Rs.66,000/- if added, would be
Rs.10,69,772/-.
15. Asset No.2 : is the site bearing No.6 measuring 30 x 40 situated at Hebbal Kempapura,
Bengaluru. The accused admits its purchase for Rs.1,32,000/- vide the sale deed at Ex.P80 dated
09.01.2004 from Sri. G. Laxman through his GPA Holder - Smt. Y. Rathnamma (the wife of the
accused). In his written arguments, the accused admits the purchase value. Admittedly, the ground
+ two floors building came to be constructed therein. PW6 claims to have evaluated the construction
cost of this building at Rs.21,12,413/- vide his report at Ex.P7. The accused questions the correctness
of the assessment made by PW6 with reference to his 13(A) schedule statement. Wherein, 17 Spl.

Rs.2,05,000/- in the year 1994-95. According to him, she has arranged the amount by selling her
golden ornaments, raising the hand loan of Rs.50,000/- from Sri. B. M. Ashwath Narayana, the loan
from a society apart getting the financial assistance from DW3 Sri. Chinnappa Reddy.

13(A) schedule is that, he has raised the loan of Rs.11,50,000/- from the HDFC Bank, took the

stating that, he has constructed the first and second floor building in the year 2005-06 at the cots of
Rs.11,50,000/- only that too, under his own self supervision. Interesting is the written arguments of
the accused. Wherein, he clearly admits the construction cost of Rs.21,12,413/- assessed by PW6 and
considered by the IO. But, his only grievance is as if, PW6 has adopted the notification of the year
1998 issued by the department of Stamps and Registration to assess the construction cost of the
ground floor of the year 1994-95. Therefore according to him, 7% of the construction cost towards
depreciation for 4 years at Rs.4,73,180/- and Rs.4,22,482/- towards 10% each for the self
supervision and overhead charges has to be deducted. He mean to say that, the IO should have
considered the total construction cost of Rs.12,16,751/- after all such deductions. In view of the 19
Spl. C.C.456/2017 above, and even if the report of PW6 is considered to be defective in nature, the
cost of construction at Rs.21,12,413/- came to be admitted by the accused is relevant.
iii) More importantly, the recitals of sale deed dated 09.01.2004 at Ex.P80 in the name of the
accused does not refer the existence of either the ground floor or the building of any kind at site
No.6. Therefore, the construction of the ground floor in the year 1994-95 or its existence as on the
date of purchase of the site by the accused is very difficult to believe. That means, it must have
constructed subsequently. However, the report of PW6 and the evidence of IO reveals the ground
floor building of 1994-95. Similarly, the evidence of the accused discloses the construction of the
first and second floors building in the year 2005-06, is contrary to the years 2004-05 and 2005-
06. Despite all these contradictions, the very defence of the accused and reasons discussed herein
above goes to establish the cost of the building more than the cost considered by the IO at
Rs.21,12,413/-. Based on the observations herein above, the entitlement for the depreciation at 7%
for 4 years cannot be accepted. Similarly, for reasons discussed on asset No.1, the deduction at 20%
as sought for by the accused towards self supervision and overhead charges needs to ignore.
Therefore, the admitted purchase price of Rs.1,32,000/- + 20 Spl. C.C.456/2017 construction cost of
Rs.21,12,413/- = 22,44,413/- stands established.

accused have entered into a memorandum of understanding (for short, the MOU) dtd 15.12.2006
